questions.question: The direction of magnetic field lines produced by a straight current-carrying wire is given by:
questions.explanation: According to Maxwell’s Right-Hand Thumb Rule, if the thumb points in the direction of current, the curled fingers give the direction of magnetic field lines.

questions.question: Inside a long current-carrying solenoid, the magnetic field is:
options: Uniform and parallel along the axis
Decreases as we move towards the ends
Increases as we move towards the ends
questions.explanation: Inside a solenoid, the magnetic field lines are in the form of parallel straight lines, indicating that the magnetic field is uniform at all points inside.

questions.question: In Fleming’s Left-Hand Rule, the middle finger represents the direction of:
questions.explanation: In the FBI left-hand mnemonic: Thumb = Force/Motion (F), Forefinger = Magnetic Field (B), Middle Finger = Electric Current (I).

questions.question: What is the function of an earth wire in domestic electrical appliances?
options: To provide a low-resistance path to the ground for leakage currents to prevent severe electric shock
To increase current capacity of appliances
To act as a backup live wire
questions.explanation: The metallic body of appliances is connected to the earth wire, ensuring that any current leakage flows safely to the ground and blows the fuse rather than shocking the user.

questions.question: Why does a spinning ice skater rotate faster when pulling their arms inward?
options: Conservation of Angular Momentum (Moment of inertia decreases, so angular velocity increases)
Air resistance decreases when arms are close
Gravitational pull increases toward the center
questions.explanation: When arms are drawn in, mass is closer to the rotation axis, decreasing moment of inertia (I). Because angular momentum L = I·ω is conserved, angular velocity ω must increase.

questions.question: If you shine red light and green light together onto a white wall, what color do your eyes perceive?
questions.explanation: In additive color mixing of light, combining red and green light stimulates the red and green cone photoreceptors in your retina, which your brain perceives as yellow.
